test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 20 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about the gradation of boiling point in a homologous series is correct?

options.text: The boiling points increase with decreasing molecular mass.
The boiling points decrease with increasing molecular mass.
The boiling points increase with increasing molecular mass.
The boiling point does not depend on molecular mass.

solution:
The correct answer is **__The boiling points increase with increasing molecular mass.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Homologous Series__**

 __
 
• ​Any homologous sequence exhibits a gradation in physical attributes as the** molecule mass rises.**
 
• This is due to the fact that when **molecule mass increases, melting and boiling points also rise**.
 
• Similar gradations can be seen in other physical attributes like **solubility in a particular solvent.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Because only **immediate dipole-induced dipole** interactions can contribute to the intermolecular forces, **alkanes have relatively low boiling points**.
 
• Because of the **carbon-chlorine polar link (+C-Cl-),** which creates a permanent dipole and adds a tiny amount to the intermolecular forces, **primary halogenoalkanes (n-alkyl halides) have somewhat higher boiling temperatures than alkanes.**
 
• Because the** N-H bond (-N-H+) **is more polar than the C-Cl bond and this permanent dipole** - permanent dipol**e interactions will result in hydrogen bonding, but not to the same extent as for alcohols, primary aliphatic amines are the** second highest boiling compounds.**
 
• **Aldehydes and isomeric ketones **are both primary aliphatic amines that are linear in structure. It would seem that the hydrogen bonding in the amines has roughly the same impact here as the permanent dipole - permanent dipole intermolecular attractive interactions caused by the polarised **carbonyl bond (+C=O-)**.
 
• 
 
Due to the additional** intermolecular tension of hydrogen bonds, alcohols (alkanols) exhibit much higher boiling temperatures than alkanes, BUT ONLY for the lower members.**

 
 
• 
 
Because there are additional >C=O... >C=0 attractions in addition to hydrogen bonding, or you could argue that there are two sites on the molecule for hydrogen bonding, again only for the lower members of the series, and dimers are easily formed for the lower members of the series, **carboxylic acids (also known as alkanoic acids) are even higher than alcohols.**
